gaps.quote: Any invertible linear transformation of $H$ or $D$ costs $O(V)$ (cited)
gaps.note: Stated too widely. Only lower-triangular invertible transformations cost O(V), because they update coordinates from last to first using earlier unchanged coordinates (the page's own justification). A general invertible matrix has no such order. Paper, Lemma matrix-shear proof (line 1425): 'A lower triangular transformation of H, or of D, costs O(V)'.

gaps.quote: The paper shows $N<2L_{\rm b}$, so $s_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}R$.
gaps.note: Inequality direction is wrong. From s_b = W_b R - N + 2L_b, s_b < W_b R requires N > 2L_b; N < 2L_b would give s_b > W_b R. The paper says 'Its deficit from W_b m is N-2L_b>0' (line 1176), so N > 2L_b.

gaps.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
gaps.note: Does not follow from 'q must not divide xi', which only constrains denominators. The paper (lines 1411-1415) avoids every denominator and the numerators of diagonal entries of invertible factors (e.g. a prime exceeding all nonzero numerators and denominators); a zero numerator is divisible by every q.

gaps.quote: Each edge of the bit network carries such a matrix.
gaps.note: The bit network, its wires, edges and the matrix on each edge are never defined on this page; the linked page covers only generic networks with roles and frames.

gaps.quote: The network's rank budget, which counts dimension changes along its edges, gives $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}R-N+2L_{\rm b}$
gaps.note: The formula is asserted with no derivation or statement of why it holds. Negative source projections and decreasing edges are never explained, so the reader cannot check the formula or see why s_b is the sum of edge ranks.
